channel.title: FIA Press Releases
channel.description: Official press releases from the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile

item.title: Refinements to the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Regulations Agreed by All Stakeholders
item.description:
Following a meeting between the FIA, Team Principals, and Power Unit Manufacturers, several refinements to the 2026 Formula 1 regulations have been agreed and will take effect from the Miami Grand Prix.
ENERGY MANAGEMENT: Adjustments to energy management parameters, including a reduction in maximum permitted recharge from 8MJ to 7MJ per lap, aimed at reducing excessive harvesting and encouraging more consistent flat-out driving. This change targets a maximum superclip duration reduced to approximately two to four seconds per lap.
Peak superclip power increased to 350kW, previously being 250kW, further reducing the time spent recharging and reducing driver workload on energy management.
The number of events where alternative lower energy limits may apply has been increased from 8 to 12 races, allowing greater adaptation to circuit characteristics.
RACE STARTS: Changes to race start procedures will be trialled at Miami before full adoption. Maximum ERS deployment will be reduced at race starts, limiting torque and improving car control in low-grip conditions.

item.title: FIA Announce Energy Management Adjustment for 2026 Japanese Grand Prix Qualifying
item.description:
Formula 1's governing body have announced a modification to the energy management parameters for Qualifying at this weekend's Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka.
Following discussions between the FIA, all 11 Formula 1 teams and the Power Unit manufacturers, it has been unanimously agreed to reduce the maximum permitted energy recharge for Qualifying at Suzuka from 9.0MJ to 8.0MJ.
The FIA stated: "To ensure that the intended balance between energy deployment and driver performance is maintained, this targeted adjustment is part of the normal process of optimisation as the new regulatory framework is further validated in real-world conditions."
No changes have been made to race energy limits for the Japanese Grand Prix. The standard 8MJ race limit remains in place for the race itself.

item.title: Technical Analysis: How Teams Are Managing Energy Deployment in 2026
item.description:
With the 2026 season now three rounds old, teams have gathered significant data on how to optimise their energy deployment strategies under the new regulations.
Mercedes data shows their car is recovering an average of 8.5MJ per lap at Monaco-style circuits, while at power circuits like Monza, recovery drops to just 4.2MJ.
Red Bull Ford has reportedly found a way to reduce their superclip phase to just 1.8 seconds per lap, recovering the full 4MJ battery capacity in fewer braking zones than their rivals. Ferrari meanwhile are averaging 6.7MJ recovery per lap across the first three events.
The data paints a picture of a grid still coming to terms with the demands of the new power unit architecture.

item.title: FIA Statement: Further Energy Management Discussions Ongoing
item.description:
The FIA, together with Formula 1 teams and Power Unit Manufacturers, continues to evaluate energy management parameters ahead of the Miami Grand Prix.
Further refinements to the recharge limits are under consideration and will be announced before the next event. The governing body has stressed that any changes will be agreed unanimously before implementation.
Teams have been asked to submit technical feedback by end of the following week.

item.title: 2026 Belgian Grand Prix: FIA Confirms Energy Limits for Spa-Francorchamps
item.description:
Ahead of this weekend's Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps, the FIA has confirmed the energy recharge limits that will apply throughout the race weekend.
For the race, the maximum permitted recharge remains at 7MJ per lap, in line with the standard limit introduced from Miami.
For qualifying, the FIA has determined that a lower limit of 6.5MJ will apply at Spa, reflecting the circuit's long straights and limited braking zones. This represents a reduction from the standard 7MJ qualifying limit.
Teams were informed of this decision on Tuesday following a technical review of circuit characteristics and power unit telemetry from previous Spa events.

item.title: WRC Rally Estonia: Energy Recovery Limits Confirmed for Hybrid Cars
item.description: Ahead of Rally Estonia, the FIA has confirmed that WRC hybrid cars will operate under a maximum energy recovery limit of 3.5MJ per stage. This applies to all Hybrid Rally1 cars competing in the event. The limit was set following analysis of stage profiles and safety considerations for spectator zones.
